newsitem.title: USA: Husband of woman killed in TWA 800 crash sues.
newsitem.headline: Husband of woman killed in TWA 800 crash sues.

text.p: The husband of a Houston woman killed in the fiery crash of TWA Flight 800 sued the airline in federal court in Houston on Friday for unspecified damages, according to court documents.
Joe Lychner lost his wife, Pam Lychner, 37, and children Shannon, 10, and Katie, 8, in the crash.
In court papers, he said the airplane they boarded on their way to Paris was improperly maintained and too old to be flying.
The Trans World Airlines Boeing 747 exploded in mid-air and plunged into the Atlantic Ocean off New York's Long Island on July 17, killing all 230 people on board.
Six months after the crash, federal officials remain uncertain whether the explosion was caused by a mechanical failure, a bomb or a missile.

Lychner's suit was filed by New York attorney Lee Kreindler, who represents dozens of families of victims from the TWA Flight 800 disaster. He also is the lead attorney in lawsuits stemming from the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Scotland.
Pam Lychner, a former TWA flight attendant and realtor, founded the victims' rights group Justice for All after she was attacked in August 1990 while showing a house to a prospective buyer.

Since the crash, Joe Lychner has been a spokesman of sorts for the victims' families, pressing federal officials to recover all the bodies and echoing families' suspicions in the days after the crash that the explosion was not an accident.
"At this point, I'm quite convinced" the explosion was not an accident, he said at the time.
In the lawsuit filed in U.S. District Court in Houston, Lychner alleged the airplane was not properly maintained and should have been retired years earlier.

The plane was sold to the government of Iran in the mid-1970s and then bought back by TWA. Designed to fly for 60,000 hours, the airplane had been operated for 101,000 hours at the time of the crash, he said in court papers.
Officials with the St. Louis, Missouri-based airline could not be reached for comment.
